html:
Hegra, also called Mada'in Salih or al-Hijr, is the ruin of a Nabataean city in the northwest of today's Saudi Arabia, near al-Ula. It thrived from about the 1st century BCE to the 1st century CE.

It was the second city of the Nabataean Kingdom after Petra, a stop on the incense road from Yemen to the Mediterranean. Over a hundred tombs are cut into the sandstone outcrops, many with carved facades and inscriptions naming their owners. Rome annexed the kingdom in 106.

The Quran tells of the people of al-Hijr, the Thamud, who were destroyed for rejecting a prophet, and for long the site was shunned. It became Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage Site in 2008 and is now opened to visitors. See also Saudi Arabia.
